note: Three problems caused the deaths. First, Jev's jump timing was arbitrary: ep2 jumped at dx 145, came down on the cactus and died; ep1 jumped at dx 382 and wasted the jump. Second, ep3 never jumped, even at dx 8. Third, in ep1 JUMP was chosen at alt 13, just before landing, and then held: a held key is never pressed again, so the dino did not jump and hit the large cactus. The extractor now tracks obstacle speed in memory and uses the measured jump arc (alt vs ms) to compute, for the first threat, when it enters and leaves the dino's span and whether jumping now is early, ok or late. It also flags whether a bird passes overhead or can be ducked under. The rules are now simple field checks: NOOP in the air (this releases the key), DUCK for duckable birds, JUMP when jumpTiming is not early. tickMs is now 30 for finer timing.
instructions:
Apply these rules in order and pick the first that matches.
1. If over is true: choose JUMP (restarts the game).
2. If player.air is true: choose NOOP. Never hold JUMP in the air (the key must be released so the next jump is a fresh press).
3. If threat is null: choose NOOP.
4. If threat.duckable is true and threat.impactMs <= 250: choose DUCK (keep choosing DUCK while this holds, until the bird has passed).
5. If threat.jumpTiming is "ok" or "late": choose JUMP.
6. Otherwise (threat.jumpTiming is "early"): choose NOOP and wait.
Notes: threat is the nearest obstacle that can hit the dino (birds flying above the dino are already excluded). jumpTiming "early" means a jump started now would come down on the obstacle; "ok" means a jump now clears it; "late" means the best moment has passed, so jump immediately anyway.

actions.description: Jump (only works from the ground with a fresh press), or restart the game
Duck under birds (hold while the bird passes)
